The enhancer-like cCRE annotation does not establish activity in the adipose proxy context; E05 reports no matching core biosample and no enhancer- or promoter-like call among those biosamples.

The candidate binding predictions disagree in allele direction: H1, H2, H3, and H5 predict stronger ref-T binding, whereas H4 predicts stronger alt-C binding. The risk allele is T, but no cited evidence connects any candidate's binding change to an adipose regulatory effect, FTO expression, or obesity.

Our recessive model showed a significant association with rs9939609 (OR: 1.56, 95% CI: 1.20; 2.02, p < 0.01) and rs1421085 (OR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.14; 2.75, p < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: In this study, we have found that the FTO rs9939609 and rs1421085 are associated to an increased risk of obesity among children and adolescents.
Variants rs17817449 and rs1421085 were significantly linked with PCOS susceptibility in the study population.
Six (4-8) years after BS, post-surgery weight was greater in carriers of the rs9939609 and rs1421085 risk genotypes.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis further verified the positive association of FTO rs1421085 with the risk of developing obesity.

After correcting for differences in age, gender and duration of illnesses, none of the variants was shown to be related to metabolic syndrome or abdominal obesity, but rs9939609, rs1421085, rs3751812 and rs8050136 were associated with body mass index.

The FTO (fat mass and obesity-associated) gene variant rs1421085 is strongly associated with an increased susceptibility to obesity in numerous populations; however, the precise mechanism behind this association concerning metabolomics is still not understood.
Individuals with the risk allele of rs1421085 gained more weight and increased BMI than those without the risk allele if they did not exercise.
